source.title: [P1] Release one-sensor prototype for procurement, assembly, and staged first power
source.body:
## Goal — owner-expanded scope (2026-11-13)

Deliver a **purchasable, fabricatable, owner-assemblable and safely staged first-power one-sensor prototype**, not merely a paper comparison. The owner explicitly directs that **every engineering hold and PAC blocking that specific one-sensor release be resolved within this Issue #47 task**, with hands-on owner participation after purchase/receipt. This supersedes the original paper-only end condition and the original blanket exclusion of future assembly/first-power *within this task*, but **does not itself authorize an order, fabrication, connection or energization**. A failed or unperformed check stays failed/unverified until addressed with evidence.

Acceptance uses **reasonable safeguards for a manually supervised, low-voltage engineering prototype**, not a universal zero-damage guarantee. Under an explicitly documented risk case, preventable operator faults such as reversed temporary leads, wrong header/adjacent-pin connections and reconnection under power can be controlled through **de-energized assembly, unambiguous net labels, manufacturer pinout checks, continuity/polarity inspection, supported/insulated connections and a no-live-rewiring rule**, rather than requiring hardware immunity. State the residual possibility of component damage. Do not turn those narrow procedural exclusions into a blanket exemption for hazardous supply/wiring behavior, sustained shorts/overheating, USB-host backfeed, or unknown voltage exposure.

This issue coordinates the full release and evidence crosswalk while preserving linked issue ownership:
- [#38](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/38) is the exact-component procurement and **owner purchase-authorization** surface. Reconcile the 31-MPN basket, seven original holds, exact quantities, sources, available instruments, and preferred $1,100 / flexible ~$1,300 budget. Use only the selected one-sensor subset and required tools; the full five-sensor production basket is out of scope.
- [#43](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/43) prepared the hand-assembled optical board manufacturing package but did **not** release fabrication. Resolve its real fit/boot/clamp/support, CAM, pinout, and fabrication-review conditions for this prototype; do not claim its closed issue released the FABRICATION HOLD.
- [#7](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/7) owns subsequent real optical characterization. For Issue #47, first-power and a functional one-sensor/USB smoke demonstration are in scope, **not** publication-grade optical calibration, five-channel capture qualification (#5), or production design (#11).
- [#45](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/45) and merged [PR #46](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/46) preserve the historical conditional paper-only S0/S1 decision, including the narrow procedural exclusions and disputed Cubic/Charizard findings; that paper decision did not grant physical admission.
- Draft [PR #48](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48) at `bcc05e36fd7bb1c62302939420a65de4582fbe52` contains the current A/B/C source screening and documents the still-incomplete former PAC-2. Continue from its verified candidate, not a new parallel implementation.

## Power architecture and bounded risk decision

**Preferred first-prototype path for owner decision:** a verified adjustable/current-limited **KORAD KA3005PE+ bench supply** as the sole operating VIN source for the assembled one-sensor fixture, with no permanent fixed adapter required for first release. Confirm physical inventory and exact model/revision first. Independently qualify its actual CV/CC, OVP/OCP, shutdown and output energy before connection; derive and record actual settings from the target load, manufacturer limits, leads and measurements. `INITIAL_CURRENT_LIMIT=UNSET` until that evidence exists.

The existing **Mean Well GST18U05-P1J fixed-adapter path is not qualified**: its 5.5–7.0 V OVP range exceeds the exposed 5.5 V supply-node ceiling. MF-R050 is not a guaranteed 3V3 fault-clearing device; Pololu 5383 is not forward OVP/current limiting. The TRACO TPP 15-105-J bare-mains module is likewise unselected and is not a finished desktop supply. Keep these findings, and **do not use either fixed-source candidate for first power**. If the owner accepts bench-supply-only as the released architecture, disposition B/C as rejected/deferred *alternatives outside the selected first-prototype build*, with recorded rationale; do not demand fault qualification of unused circuits as a prerequisite. If the owner requires fixed-adapter operation in this release, develop and qualify a real coordinated source/protection implementation first, including relevant mains safety. Do not silently decide this owner trade-off.

The essential hardware safety case for **the selected physical configuration** must cover within defensible measured/derived operating margins:
- Source maximum/minimum voltage including load steps and startup; credible current/energy cutoff and conductor/contact thermal limits; power-off, sudden load and short response; no invented current-limit setting.
- External 3V3 branch loading, wiring/short exposure and protection-or-procedural controls. Respect the Teensy regulator's external load budget and the optical IC ratings.
- Correct 3.3 V-only logic/GPIO, input/output polarity and physical harness support; no exposed conductor or connector mix-up hidden by color convention.
- Separate external VIN and USB VBUS domains, physically verified VIN/VUSB separation before dual-source use, USB host protection/backfeed and powered-off signal injection. Never substitute a paperwork signoff for necessary unpowered and powered measurements.
- Optical board physical fit, hand-assembly feasibility, accessible probes, strain relief and the **owner-approved noncontact optical shroud and independently supported bench mount** described below. Neither the detector, shroud, clamp, nor cabling may contact/load the display glass in the intended operating envelope.

A physical prototype may retain **disclosed bounded residual risks**, including failure of an individual component during an abnormal fault, provided the owner explicitly accepts them and the connected source, wiring, USB host, and operating procedure have a reasoned safety case. A manual check is not a guarantee; any unresolved credible serious safety exposure is a stop.

## Owner mechanical choice — noncontact first-prototype mount (2026-11-13)

**Approved: Option 1, independently supported noncontact bench mount.** The first one-sensor prototype may use an **opaque optical shroud positioned near, but not contacting, the display**, carried by an independent stable stand/fixture. Retain the **upright SFH 203**, its existing anode/cathode orientation, 50 × 44 mm optical PCB outline, copper/layout, and no-mounting-hole design. The selected optical PCB does not need a contact boot pressing against the glass. The goal is a safe first functional demonstration; repeatable contact geometry, boot compression, display contact-force characterization and publication-grade optical mount calibration belong to [Issue #7](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/7) if needed later.

**Conditions for clearing the specific optical mechanical/fabrication hold:**
1. Produce a dimensioned support/shroud concept, using a freestanding arm, bench stand, or other **independent support** that carries the PCB, detector, shroud and cable loads without transferring them to the display. Define a safe board-edge clamp/holder and strain relief; the PCB has no approved mounting holes. Keep probe points, trim adjustment, connector mating and the underside accessible. Do not change the PCB outline, detector orientation or copper without another owner decision.
2. Provide a measurable **positive air gap** between the closest shroud/detector/PCB/hardware surface and the display glass, including tolerance, setup uncertainty, adjustment, ordinary fixture flex and cable movement. Record the smallest measured gap and how it was checked (for example, documented fixture geometry with a noncontact gauge, scale or safe spacer on a mockup). Specify a stop/reposition condition if the gap could close. Do not invent a universal numerical minimum or claim a gap passed before inspection.
3. Demonstrate optical geometry plausibility before fabrication: position within the SFH 203 acceptance cone, appropriate opaque baffle/aperture, minimal ambient-light intrusion and no vignetting of the target patch. Verify the stand/shroud can be assembled without loading the photodiode leads, solder joints or glass. If required fit measurements are not available until parts arrive, distinguish **design-stage feasibility** from **post-assembly verified fit** and retain the latter hold.
4. Retain the native KiCad/ERC/DRC, Gerber/Excellon, artwork, source hashes, BOM/MPN and supplier readiness checks from #43. Fabrication clearance requires evidence for the **chosen noncontact geometry plus CAD/CAM/DFM**, not a contact-force test. Fabrication/order still needs owner authorization via #38.
5. After owner assembly, verify the physical air gap over intended motion and cable service, shroud stability, safe glass separation, acceptable ambient-light rejection (dark/bright and ambient variation), and a basic observable SFH 203 → TIA → comparator/EDGE optical response under the separately authorized staged power procedure. A dark/bright functional response is a **smoke-test result**, not the repeatability, full luminance, T50 or calibration evidence required by #7.

**Rationale:** The earlier boot compression/contact-force blocker applies to a **contact** geometry. An independently supported shroud removes the intended display-contact load path while preserving the electrically reviewed upright-sensor board. Rejecting the noncontact option in favor of a fully characterized contact boot would add work that is not needed for the initial bench prototype. This choice does not waive mechanical stability, optical signal verification, fabricated-board inspection, or first-power safety gates.

## Revised product acceptance criteria — governing PAC1–PAC6

1. **PAC-1 — Selected one-sensor topology and design decision.** Verify native CAD, Teensy revision-dependent power/USB path, optical board/harness and real instrument inventory. Select or explicitly defer the power-source architecture through an owner decision; document why excluded A/B/C alternatives are not necessary for this first prototype. Resolve in-scope technical design contradictions and capture the decision with rejected alternatives, failure modes and invariants in BENCH-005 and canonical docs.
2. **PAC-2 — Practical bounded first-power safety case.** For the *selected* path, establish source and rail voltage, load/current limit, energy/time, rated lead/contact/branch, startup/transient and thermal controls with source-backed and, where needed, dummy-load/measured evidence. Map plausible miswire, reverse, offboard short, cross-rail, open-return, hotplug and USB faults. Assign each to **hardware**, **measured operating envelope**, **mandatory procedural inspection**, or **explicitly owner-accepted residual risk** with clear stop conditions. Do not require proof of zero damage for every hypothetical fault or full closed dynamic simulation of rejected B/C circuits. Do not classify untested observed behavior as PASS.
3. **PAC-3 — Procurement and fabrication readiness.** Reconcile existing inventory and every needed exact one-sensor component/tool, including the seven historical sourcing holds; confirm MPN, pinout, package, lifecycle exception when applicable, sourceability, price and ordered quantity, and no silent substitutions. Resolve the **noncontact independent mount/shroud** design-stage clearance, stability, access, ambient-light and mechanical fit criteria above, plus native optical PCB CAM/manufacturability and inspection limits; contact-boot compression and glass contact force are not required for this first-prototype fabrication decision. Deliver **one exact purchase/fabrication packet** with cleared items and owner-authorized baskets under #38. No order or PCB fabrication without the owner's explicit approval.
4. **PAC-4 — Owner assembly and unpowered inspection.** Supply a complete hand-solder/assembly sequence, suitable tools and build photos/inspection checklist; record actual received board revision and component markings, noncontact shroud/stand fit, minimum measured glass gap over intended adjustment/motion, no loading on detector leads or board, orientation, polarity, grounded return, supported/labelled cables, isolation, and no-short continuity measurements. The owner performs physical steps and supplies evidence; no remote agent may claim receipt, soldering or test execution.
5. **PAC-5 — Bounded staged energization.** Establish and execute a single owner-approved, **conditional G0–G4/S0–S4** first-power and connection procedure based on BENCH-002/SPEC-X-004. Start with disconnected source/dummy-load qualification; then Teensy-only, additional board/LED/buffer loads, USB VBUS-only and combined-source/Android operation **in the verified dependency order**. Each stage has numeric/measurable entry criteria, current/voltage/source settings, independent measurement points, expected results, immediate shutoff triggers, and retained actual results. Once the owner approves a fully bounded plan, successful recorded gates may permit advancement **without redundant separate approvals**; a failed gate or materially changed configuration stops until reassessed. Physical NOT_RUN states become PASS only on observed evidence.
6. **PAC-6 — Demonstrated prototype handoff and hold reconciliation.** Obtain and record stable one-sensor power, appropriate 5V/3V3 rails, no unsafe USB backfeed, USB enumeration in its intended role, **a positive measured noncontact glass clearance, acceptable basic ambient-light rejection, and a basic observable optical/signal path** if physically achievable under the approved stage. Record any functional failures and bound their implications honestly. Cross-reference #38/#43/#7, close or explicitly disposition every engineering hold blocking the *selected one-sensor* purchase/assembly/first-power path, preserve residual risks and operating instructions, and hand back the working prototype acceptance record. This is **not** five-channel or publication-grade measurement qualification.

## Execution and authorization gates

- This is an **elevated-risk, multi-stage single task**. A documentation-only PR does not close it. No test requiring parts in hand may be marked PASS before actual parts, assembly and test. Hardware work is owner-performed or explicitly owner-directed.
- Codex first returns a **read-only revised plan** reconciled against this expanded scope, current PR #48, #38/#43/#7, and the process pin. ChatGPT must approve the materially revised plan before further implementation; use the existing verified worktree/branch unless identity/drift requires reassessment.
- Preserve process revision `e2afa055d1126763c69f0e0392d25b86bab98014` for #47. Do not alter historical task pins. Require independent final full-diff Standards/Spec/Cubic (or non-author) review, applicable source/native CAD/CI validation, and final ChatGPT readiness review.
- **Procurement/PCB fabrication requires specific owner basket authorization.** A budget target or desire to proceed does not authorize orders. The user handles payment/orders unless separately authorized through an appropriate action.
- **Assembly and staged first power require owner approval of the actual bounded procedure and successful earlier gates**, not a universal approval to connect hardware. A reviewed plan may batch-condition subsequent stage authorizations; stop on failed or unverified prerequisites, unexpected current/voltage/heat, or USB backfeed.
- Keep the present `INITIAL_CURRENT_LIMIT=UNSET`, S0–S4 NOT_RUN/UNVERIFIED, procurement/power-use holds and FABRICATION HOLD **until their own evidence and approvals are obtained**. Never remove a safety hold just to mark the issue complete. When each is satisfied, update its precise state and evidence without retaining redundant holds.
- No automatic merge, issue closure, checkout/order, unsafe mains assembly, or fabricated simulation/physical evidence. The owner controls material decisions, purchases, hands-on assembly and merge.

## Historical conclusions retained

The Issue #45 paper route considered S0 source qualification and conditional Teensy-only S1 feasible under narrow procedural exclusions but did not establish a numerical source envelope or physical release. Issue #47's first investigation ([PR #48](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48)) found the present fixed-adapter path fails its overvoltage screen; TPS25947 and TPS26600 leave narrow static OVLO margin at stated ripple sensitivities, and the LTC4368 external-FET alternative remains an unverified circuit proposal. Simulations of active protectors were not successful; no physical source, thermal, EMC, fault, optical or USB qualification was claimed. These outcomes and the original disputed external review evidence remain recorded in BENCH-005 and linked prior task records. The new owner direction accepts **reasonable supervised-prototype risk**, not unqualified fixed-source operation or host backfeed.

## Supervised prototype execution checkpoint and G0 decision package

Candidate: `814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd`; base: `be110a8eea18edd6c844abd8386d9670ee4a6235`; process: `e2afa055d1126763c69f0e0392d25b86bab98014`. Existing branch/worktree and draft PR #48 retained. This is an engineering checkpoint, **not completion of the physical PACs**.

### 1. Concrete G0 decision requested

Accept or amend this exact construction proposal for the first supervised one-sensor prototype:

1. **KA3005PE+ only** → Pomona 73093-2/-0 with Remington 18UL1007STRRED25/18UL1007STRBLA25, maximum 1 m per source lead → two independently held WAGO 221-412 potentials → MF-R050 → Pololu 5383 → AMASS XT30U-F.G.Y/M.G.Y → socketed DEV-20360 VIN/GND. Source positive enters 5V_IN/F1 pin 1; no L721A/GST18U05-P1J fitted or parallel source. Retain their original failure evidence; fixed-adapter B/C alternatives are deferred outside this selected first-build scope.
2. Adafruit 1606 offboard carrier, two SSW-124-01-G-S sockets at C4–C27/G4–G27, direct supported power wires rather than assumed copper-strip ampacity, covered joints/insulating supports and separately strain-relieved module/cables. Pin map and exact buffer/LED/passive assembly restrictions are in the [construction instructions](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/blob/814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd/hardware/prototype/power-usb/bench-assembly.md) and [drawing](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/blob/814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd/hardware/prototype/power-usb/bench-assembly.svg).
3. **Explicit source-lead decision:** these are owner-terminated plugs, a departure from the factory-terminated preference. Accept only with correct wire attachment, cup insulation, mating/retention, continuity and actual current/thermal qualification. Suitable owned factory leads may be proposed by exact identity/construction review; no silent substitution.
4. Preserve the optical PCB, upright SFH 203, analog values and geometry. Use the independently supported [noncontact mount proposal](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/blob/814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd/hardware/prototype/optical/bench-mount.md). The 5 mm nominal gap and derived 2.10 mm static indicated screen are configuration-specific proposed allocations, not measured clearance. Establish actual geometry/tolerance/movement evidence and final numerical limit before fabrication release; post-assembly gap remains separately observed. No contact-boot force/compression gate.
5. Accept only the narrow supervised procedural controls for reversed temporary leads, wrong/adjacent header pins and live rewiring: all rail assembly/changes de-energized, manufacturer pinouts, labels at both ends, independent continuity/polarity/isolation checks, supported insulated terminations and no live rail rewiring. **Residual component damage remains possible** despite these checks.
6. No blanket waiver for excessive source voltage/energy, sustained unsafe conductor/contact/IC heating, unknown 3V3 short behavior, USB backfeed or unintended power through GPIO/probe earth/open return. These require measured/derived bounded controls, and a credible serious unresolved hazard stops release.
7. Keep the separate actual USB/HID/vendor session and manual physical display-light session. Optional bench firmware supplies only the guarded steady LED load/input pin configuration; it does not certify optical acquisition or HID-caused rendering. Bus-T0, calibrated latency, Issue #6 renderer, #7 calibration and five-channel qualification remain outside this smoke release.

**G0 acceptance would adopt the bounded design/risk basis only. It would not authorize any order, print/fabrication, assembly, source qualification, connection, flashing or energization.** Those retain their own explicit gates.

### 2. PAC-1 through PAC-6

| PAC | Prepared engineering/source evidence | Remaining obligation and present disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAC-1 | Concrete direct-bench wiring/carrier, unchanged optical source, source-backed limits and deferred alternatives recorded. | **OPEN:** owner G0 acceptance, actual received source/Teensy/U4/manual identities and the still-needed instrument/accessory selections. The owner-declared zero-electronics inventory is retained. |
| PAC-2 | Fault-control map covers reverse/miswire, 5V/3V3 shorts, cross-rail/powered-off injection, open return, hotplug and USB; measurement/energy/thermal method and stop rules recorded. | **INCOMPLETE:** no measured source/rail/current/cutoff/energy/thermal envelope, actual conductor/contact/branch proof or reviewed numerical current setting. Original fixed adapter still fails OVP. Unused B/C dynamic envelopes are deferred, not passed and not a bench-only prerequisite. |
| PAC-3 | [Exact core/support/equipment/PCB packet](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/38#issuecomment-6873763863); canonical support lifecycle-exception dispositions integrated; native CAD and retained CAM identities verified. | **OPEN:** the zero-inventory minimum quantities plus unresolved equipment/accessory choices, exact eLab offer and seller fulfillment/packaging at order time, completed chosen noncontact design-fit/tolerance/DFM evidence and separate owner G1 component/PCB approvals. |
| PAC-4 | Assembly/pinout/inspection sequence and [blank commissioning record](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/blob/814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd/hardware/prototype/power-usb/commissioning.template.json). | **NOT_RUN:** owner receipt/assembly, photos, actual markings, pin/polarity/continuity/insulation, VIN/VUSB cut/isolation, supported cable/holder and minimum-gap observations. G2 ungranted. |
| PAC-5 | Ordered S0, S1, S2, S3a, S3b, S4a, G4/S4b dependencies, expected observations and stop conditions. | **NOT_RUN:** actual instrument-specific S0 protocol, source results, numerical stage settings/exposure intervals and independent review before G3. Successful explicitly authorized conditional stages may advance; failure/configuration change stops. |
| PAC-6 | Implemented manual black/white page and tested optional bench firmware, separate optical/USB evidence records. | **NOT_RUN:** real stable rails, safe USB isolation, intended Full-Speed enumeration/identity, actual HID press/release and vendor exchange, measured positive gap, ambient controls and real SFH203→TIA→EDGE response. No synthetic substitute. |

### 3. Hold-by-hold disposition

| Hold | Exact disposition / evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Seven historical acquisition HOLDs | Prior evaluation-only clearance retained; no rollback solely for missing Active lifecycle. Exact identities unchanged. |
| New support lifecycle/fit screen | Canonical component-level exception dispositions prepared under SPEC-X-001; lifecycle stays UNVERIFIED, bounded search limitation retained. Physical use remains held. |
| Inventory / quantity / exact order | Declared zero prototype electronics/PSU/instruments; core minimum 27 identities/33 units, source ×1 and DMM/access needed. Only subsequent acquisitions/accessory capability, actual MOQ/packaging and seller offer require reconciliation. |
| Owner purchase authority | CLOSED GATE: G1 exact baskets via #38; budget is not permission. |
| Optical fabrication | HOLD: substantiate selected noncontact design-stage geometry/tolerances/access/opacity/plausibility and DFM, then separate PCB authorization. Retained CAM/native checks remain valid. |
| Contact-boot compression/force | Not applicable to the approved noncontact first build; no intended glass load path. |
| Actual mount/glass clearance | UNVERIFIED: confirm design allocations, then observe assembled minimum gap over intended adjustment/flex/cable/tap motion. Fail closed if gap can close. |
| Receipt/assembly/unpowered checks | NOT_RUN; owner G2, actual part/board revision, photos, continuity/polarity/insulation and supported returns. |
| Source-only S0 | NOT_RUN: exact unit/manual/instruments, rated dummy fixture, approved protocol, actual CV/CC/OVP/OCP/peak/current/time/energy and thermal captures. |
| Initial/stage current limits | **UNSET** until source evidence, load/branch ratings and independent settings review. |
| 3V3 branch and sustained faults | OPEN: actual U4/regulator/branch behavior and bounded heating/exposure; do not credit MF-R050 as guaranteed clearing. |
| VIN/VUSB, partial-power and host backfeed | UNVERIFIED: physical separation and approved off/on leakage/rail tests before Android. No paper-only release. |
| Staged S1–S4 / G3 and G4 | NOT_RUN; numerical procedures and applicable owner approvals required. |
| Real USB/HID/vendor and manual optical smoke | NOT_RUN; retain actual observations, failures and diagnostic/raw evidence separately. |
| Fixed-adapter B/C | Deferred alternative pending G0 bench-only decision; original OVP failure/unknown envelopes remain, no silent qualification. |
| Five-channel / bus-T0 / calibrated optical / renderer / production | Retain under existing downstream issues; not required to prove this bounded independent-session smoke result. |

### 4. Immediate owner input

A. Record G0 acceptance or specific amendments to the proposal and residual-risk scope above, including the custom source leads.

B. Retain the owner's [zero-electronics/PSU/test-instrument inventory](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/38#issuecomment-6850478344) and available soldering/flux/solder/ESD/P1S categories. Report only changes since that statement. Identify borrowed or proposed instrument access, unresolved assembly accessory capabilities, target chassis/cradle dimensions and available stand/holder/materials. Source/Teensy markings are receipt evidence, not assumed owned.

C. Review component/equipment acquisition and PCB fabrication as separate later G1 decisions once their packets are concrete. No later physical gate is approved by G0 alone.

Native [validation evidence](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48#issuecomment-6873744514) and [initial independent full-diff findings](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48#issuecomment-6873805538) are published. [Final full-diff Standards and Spec reviews](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48#issuecomment-6874036857) both PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the source proposal, and [final validation/local Cubic/CI evidence](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/pull/48#issuecomment-6874054195) is published. These do not satisfy the open physical PACs or grant owner approvals. `INITIAL_CURRENT_LIMIT=UNSET`; no physical work has been performed or claimed. Issue #47 stays open and PR #48 stays draft/unmerged.

Inventory correction applied to this checkpoint: the later owner comments establish zero prototype electronics and test instruments, superseding the earlier DMM snapshot. The current canonical procurement guidance and purchase packet now agree; historical scenario arithmetic remains labeled historical.

## OWNER DECISION — G0 ARCHITECTURE ACCEPTED (2026-11-14)

**Decision:** The owner explicitly approved the [G0 decision package](https://github.com/whatobiplays/screen-latency-tool/issues/47#issuecomment-6873827927) in the ChatGPT review of draft PR #48 at candidate `814d5a1311a6072cbb05333ad215dc7b17781cdd`. **G0 architecture/risk selection: ACCEPTED.** This is a material engineering decision, **not** an acceptance of any unperformed physical PAC, and **not** purchase, assembly, first-power, firmware-flashing, or merge authorization.

### Accepted first-prototype configuration

1. **Power:** Sole regulated operating source is the qualified **KORAD KA3005PE+ bench supply**, with no parallel or connected GST18U05-P1J/L721A fixed-adapter path. Proposed source connections are Pomona `73093-2` red / `73093-0` black and Remington `18UL1007STRRED25` / `18UL1007STRBLA25` 18 AWG stranded leads, **no more than 1 m per lead**, into two **separate, mechanically supported** WAGO `221-412` splices. The positive feed enters `5V_IN` / MF-R050 F1 pin 1, then `MF-R050 → Pololu 5383 → AMASS XT30U-F.G.Y/M.G.Y → socketed DEV-20360 VIN`, with an explicitly supported common return. Pololu is reverse-voltage/reverse-current protection, not forward OVP or CC; the PTC is not assumed to clear all downstream faults.
2. **Construction:** Adafruit 1606 offboard carrier, two Samtec `SSW-124-01-G-S` sockets at the documented positions, direct rated and insulated supply/return conductors rather than assumed copper-strip ampacity, supported Pololu module, covered joints, strain relief, and manufacturer/pinout-verified buffer, LED, and USB interfaces.
3. **Owner-terminated source leads expressly accepted as a prototype-only exception to the factory-terminated preference.** The exact **Pomona 73093 is a solderless push-tab termination** (not a solder-cup connection): manufacturer specifies **18–22 AWG**, strip **4–6 mm**, push and hold the tab, insert stripped wire, then release. Correct the source-lead assembly instructions and inspection checklist accordingly; require no exposed strands, secure mechanical retention, unpowered polarity/continuity and current/thermal qualification. Do not solder or apply a solder-cup instruction to these plugs. Manufacturer: https://www.pomonaelectronics.com/sites/default/files/d73093_001.pdf. The approval does not equate the connector's headline current rating with the assembled lead's continuous rating.
4. **Optics:** Preserve the unchanged 50×44 mm optical PCB, upright SFH 203, original electrical design and independently supported **noncontact** shroud/stand. The 5 mm nominal / calculated 2.10 mm indicated gap threshold is a **proposal only**; prove the actual tolerance/movement/measurement case before fabrication release and measure the assembled minimum clearance later. Contact-boot compression and display-contact force are outside this first build.
5. **Smoke demonstration:** Keep the Android USB/HID/vendor test separate from slow, manual real-display black/white optical transitions; the Issue #6 renderer, calibrated timing, full five-channel design, and Issue #7 optical calibration remain downstream.

### Accepted risk model and protected invariants

- **Procedural controls are acceptable** for narrowly bounded miswire, reverse temporary-lead, adjacent-header, and live-reconnection hazards: all wiring changes de-energized; net labels at both ends; manufacturer pin-map checks; independent unpowered polarity, isolation and continuity checks; supported insulated connections; **no live rewiring**. The owner accepts that an inadvertent mistake or abnormal component failure may still damage a component.
- **Not waived:** uncontrolled source voltage/current/energy, sustained unsafe conductor/contact/regulator heating, unbounded 3V3 branch shorts, open-return/alternate ground paths, powered-off injection, VIN/VUSB bridging, USB-host backfeed, or serious unresolved hazards. These must be bounded through the required physical tests and independently reviewed S0–S4 numerical admission limits. An unqualified physical configuration remains blocked.
- **Rejected/deferred alternatives:** No fixed GST18U05-P1J first-power path (previous OVP screen failed); no requirement to qualify unused B/C circuits or develop a new protector PCB before the selected bench-only one-sensor prototype. Historical failure and disputed review evidence remain intact.
